properties.decision: Remove `default:` from `Artifact.granularity` and `Artifact.volatility` in schema/build.yaml. Nothing else: no code change, no backfill, no change to the content hash, no tolerance added to the round-trip gate.
properties.name: Artifact.granularity and .volatility declare no schema default — the safe reading is supplied by the reader, so absence stays honest
properties.rationale:
Anthony's word, 2026-08-15, choosing a FOURTH option over the three music_graph proposed in F23 — and this settles F23 and the round-trip gate's behaviour as ONE decision, which was his framing before it was anyone's analysis.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED IT: the safe reading already lives in the reader. coverage.rs:209 reads granularity with `.unwrap_or("atomic")`; drift.rs:436 reads volatility with `.unwrap_or("stable")`. Those are the only two readers. So the schema default was redundant with the code — it changed no report's verdict, and its only observable effect was to write an intent nobody expressed onto every Artifact at import. Proven by the counterweights, which are the point: the two absence cases in tests/artifact_intent.rs (`graph_with(None)`, `graph_with_granularity(None)`) passed BEFORE this change because the schema injected the value and pass AFTER it because the reader supplies it, unchanged either way.

WHY NOT THEIR THREE. (a) backfill on import and open — migrates a store once, but writes values nobody chose into every consumer store permanently, which is the exact erosion cap:defaults-are-not-serialized exists to prevent. (b) exclude default-valued properties from the content hash — their own preference, and the one route this design has already argued CANNOT work: absence would come to mean "nobody said OR somebody chose the default", the distinction lost in the act of protecting it, and it would weaken the hash for the 71 properties that legitimately keep defaults. (c) have --import print what it defaulted — leaves the gate red and the restore broken, and only makes the blocked commit self-explanatory.

⚠️ IT REVERSES A DELIBERATE KEEP, and that is the honest cost. BL-198 removed ten of 81 defaults on 2026-08-10 and KEPT these two, on the reasoning that `stable` is the safe reading. That reasoning was correct and is untouched; what is new is the measurement that the reader already holds it. The reflex being corrected is the same one BL-198 named from the other side — there it was "single-valued means informationless", wrong three times in ten; here it is "the safe reading must be stored", wrong because storing it converts a fallback into an assertion.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: nothing already written moves. reflow2's own Artifacts keep their values, so its export does not churn and its own round trip stays clean. It does not address F24 (the latent surface never re-probes after a CLI restore), which sits on the same restore path and is a separate defect.
